problem: States as fact that the 2026 manuscript 'proves' the zero-free half-plane; per the timeline it is an unverified AI claim.
corrected: A 2026 AI-produced manuscript claims a zero-free half-plane for finite-order Hecke $L$-functions over $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ and transfers it to Dirichlet $L$-functions.

problem: Over Q only the finite-order Hecke L-functions are Dirichlet L-functions; the infinite-order ones are vertical shifts L(s - i tau, chi).
corrected: $L$-functions of Hecke characters (Größencharaktere) on ideals of a number field. Hecke (1918) proved their analytic continuation and functional equation. Over $\mathbb Q$ they are Dirichlet $L$-functions, up to a shift $s\mapsto s-i\tau$.

problem: 'The maximum size is sqrt N + O(N^{1/4})' claims a two-sided error O(N^{1/4}); only the upper bound has that error. The known lower bound for all N is sqrt N - O(N^{0.2625}) (Singer sets plus Baker-Harman-Pintz prime gaps).
corrected: A set where all pairwise sums $a+b$ ($a\le b$) are distinct. In $[1,N]$ the maximum size is at most $\sqrt N + O(N^{1/4})$ and at least $\sqrt N - O(N^{0.2625})$; whether it is $\sqrt N + O_\varepsilon(N^\varepsilon)$ is Erdős problem #30, with a 1000-dollar prize.
